messages:
sophia: Thinking about adding a tenant-level read-routing preference flag so product teams can opt into 'in-region-only' reads for data residency. Thoughts on API surface + safety?

mike: What's the failure mode? If the resident region is overloaded do we fail open to other regions or return an error?

sophia: Prefer fail-closed (error) for consent-required tenants, but we should support a 'soft' preference that permits fallback with an explicit telemetry tag and audit log.

alexa: We already have routing weights per-tenant. Proposal: add an enum read_residency with values {strict_residency, regional_prefer, global}.
  - strict_residency -> no cross-region fallback (errors if local unavailable)
  - regional_prefer -> try local, then fallback to compatible region with a 'fallback_reason' tag
  - global -> route for best latency/cost.
  Also include a fallback_policy field to express whether fallbacks are logged/auditable.

jordan: Strict_residency will raise error rates during regional outages; that needs to be an explicit SLA/paid option. Also: cache inefficiency  per-region prefix/KV caches mean misses spike for strict tenants.

carol: Operationally we can expose a 'residency_safety_score' in the console: estimated error ratio under N% load and expected cost delta. Useful for sales/compliance.

ops-bot: deploy-check: new enum requires config migration. Suggested transform: existing customers default -> regional_prefer. Plan: canary rollout in us-east for 24h then 10% global.

mike: For strict tenants, we should also provide a pre-warm/priming workflow for their KV/prefix caches in the resident region to avoid cold-start spikes. Could be a console action.

sanjay: Quick sim numbers: strict_residency -> +18% p99 latency and +12% infra cost in our synthetic tenant-mix (I/O bound model). I'll post more detailed sims in the follow-up doc.

sophia: Next steps: 1) define API flag shape, 2) console toggle + billing tag, 3) migration plan + canary, 4) compliance audit log. @alexa and @sanjay to own API + sims. I'll open RFC follow-up issue.

alexa: :thumbsup: I'll draft the API shape. Quick sketch for config: ```json
{"read_residency": "strict_residency", "fallback_policy": "none"}
```
  where fallback_policy can be one of [none, prefer_local, allow_global] and we emit a fallback audit event when fallback_policy != none.

carol: Also require an audit entry whenever fallback happens with tenant_id + timestamp + reason. Compliance will insist on that for EU/regulated customers.

jordan: Agree. We should also supply a test harness that can replay production traffic with strict_residency toggled to measure real-world impact before SLA change.

sophia: Thanks  I'll create the issue with tasks and owners. Will tag compliance + billing.
